cautions: Preserve the supplied outline and exhibits; unresolved evidence bindings are production issues, not permission to rename slots, repair evidence silently or invent missing values.

Several outline needs, table references and mandatory citations have no matching evidence key, including {F052}, {T011}, {T012}, {S002}, {F008}, {S013}, {T022}, {F018}, {F021} and {F004}; flag these for deterministic binding resolution before publication.
Producer claims also contain unresolved aliases and scope errors; use authoritative facts and valid series rather than copying those claims, and keep {K002} explicitly within database bytes.

The owner's declaration settles ownership and use rights; ignore contradictory legacy recommendations for new rights clearance, while retaining de-identification or aggregation as product preparation and distinguishing rights from operational execution approval.
No current whole-estate invoice or carrying-cost baseline is supplied; {F019} is an estimated reference-list-price monthly upper bound, not current spend, realised savings or guaranteed net benefit.
Keep {F005} and {F006} scoped to database reclaimability before pricing, and {F021} scoped to bytes addressed by cost strategies; do not sum overlapping opportunities or equate tiering with deletion.

The evidence describes object duplicate-candidate matching inconsistently across the fact scope and glossary; retain candidate status and require content-hash confirmation without inventing a reconciled matching method.

No-write age does not measure read demand, absence of personal-data markers does not prove absence of personal data, and required-looking fields are heuristic rather than necessarily enforced constraints.

Keep database cleanup bounded by {F005} and {F006}, measure outcomes against {F019} and the condition baselines, and distinguish proposed responsibilities from authorised execution or promised savings.

chapter_notes.chapter6: Lead with separate inventories: news scripts {F080}, stations {F081} and scripted dates {F082}; model-read transcripts {F070} and {F071}; and workbench registrations {F090}, {F091} and {F092}. Make the sequence an explicit planning judgement requiring canonicalisation, completeness checks, de-identification or aggregation and buyer-side validation; dimensional readiness establishes neither market demand nor revenue, and rights are already settled.
chapter_notes.chapter8: Lead with the decisions in {T013}, grounding storage priorities in {F036}, {F034} and unreadable buckets {F033}, with {F019} for bounded financial benefit and {F060} for the audio preparation opportunity. Ask for approval of accountable verification and preparation work using the table's actual roles and checks, without inventing unseen row details or implying that approval, migration, deletion or product release has already occurred.
chapter_notes.chapter9: Lead with the coverage boundary using {F003} against {F002}, unreadable buckets {F033}, enumerated file shares {F040} and {F041}, and transcripts still unread {F075}. Pair each gap with its stated closing measurement, including complete-pass sampling checks, provider reconciliation, file fingerprinting, script-language reading and corpus overlap joins; use {T036} only for authoring-role transparency, not independent validation of the estate.
chapter_notes.compare: Compare {O1}, {O2} and {O3} on estimated benefit and required verification, with {F019} identifying the overall priced monthly upper bound. Recommend validating object-store tiering first and hashing duplicate candidates before removal, without calling list-price estimates invoice savings or inventing a current carrying-cost baseline.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S001: Lead with database concentration in {S001}, using {F004} and {K002} to explain where database-scale investigation should focus. Treat the exhibit as a prioritisation map, not evidence that the largest database causes every aggregate condition finding or holds most whole-estate bytes.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S002: Lead with completeness and damage as preparation priorities using {S002}, {F009} and {F008}, alongside exact duplication {F007} and sampled personal-data markers {F010}. Keep row, sampled-row and byte denominators distinct, and do not add overlapping condition measures or extend database ratios to the whole estate.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S003: Lead with {S003} to show that object-store tiering and duplicate reconciliation dominate addressed bytes, supported by {F036}, {K009} and {F034}. Explain that addressed bytes include cheaper storage rather than only removal, and that no-write age does not establish absence of reads.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S004: Lead with the whole-estate distribution in {S004}, anchored by {F050}, {F030} and {F040}, so the owner sees that object storage and file shares dominate capacity. Keep database holdings in view through {F052}, without presenting rounded store totals as an exact reconciliation.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S005: Lead with object-store concentration in {S005} and {F038}, using {F030} as the store denominator. Direct attention to the largest buckets for operational review, without implying that size alone establishes waste or suitability for archival.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S010: Lead with the language-folder distribution in {S010}, anchored by recorded duration {F060}, estimated speech {F061} and estimated music {F062}. Show where a bounded audio pilot could draw material, but describe non-music duration as a detector-based proxy rather than verified usable speech.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S011: Lead with variation in folder-language agreement from {S011}, explaining the labelled-window denominator through {F072} and the declined share through {F066}. The takeaway is to prioritise language review before packaging, not to interpret model agreement as human verification, transcription accuracy or intelligibility.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S012: Lead with station-level script holdings in {S012}, supported by {F080} and {F081}, and place the archive's temporal coverage in context using {F082} and {F083}. Treat broadcast language as station metadata, not a language reading of each script, and avoid implying continuous daily coverage.
chapter_notes.exhibit_S013: Lead with bulletin-hour coverage conditional on scripted days in {S013}, using {T033} and {T032} for detailed traceability. Explain that activity on days carrying scripts is not evidence of complete coverage across the archive's date span or of a script at every configured hour.
chapter_notes.risks: Lead with risks to decision confidence rather than reopening rights: incomplete database coverage {F003} against {F002}, sampled personal-data markers {F010}, duplicate candidates {F034} and list-price savings {F019}. Require operational dependency checks, retrieval-cost validation and product-specific privacy preparation, without labelling all cold bytes unused, all candidate copies disposable or all marked rows unsuitable for reuse.

planner.title_direction: Frame the estate-wide account as an owner decision on where to reduce carrying costs and which products to prepare first, separating measured holdings, bounded savings and remaining preparation.

findings.fix: Replace the placeholders with {F082} and {F018}; confirm F001→Databases 20, F033→40 unreadable buckets, F035→5.0% duplicate-candidate objects, F065→20.4% music windows, F083→1,432 days, K004, K011, K012 bind before build.
findings.issue: Two figures are written with placeholder tokens rather than fact ids: {F082} here (and in chapter6.points) stands for the 226 scripted dates (F082), and {F018} in paper.sections.chapter7 stands for the 8 candidates (F018). The draft also cites F001, F033, F035, F065, F083, K004, K011 and K012 whose evidence keys appear only under redacted names; the quantities match their labels, but the binder must confirm every one resolves.

findings.fix: State the scope: 'about 15.2 GiB (4.3%) looks reclaimable inside the databases before pricing; the 54.1 GiB cold-table move is tiering, not removal' — or drop 'bounded' and cite both figures with their labels. Apply the same to paper.sections.actions.
findings.issue: 'Database cleanup is bounded by {F005} GiB' (15.2 GiB) sits in the same pack as the cold-table move O3 at 54.1 GiB and index removal at 14.0 GiB, both database strategies. The owner will read 15.2 as contradicting 54.1 unless the two scopes are distinguished.

findings.fix: Write 'declined to label {F066} of speech windows' here and in paper.sections.exhibit_S011.
findings.issue: F066 is labelled as a share of speech windows, but the draft says 'the model declined to label {F066}' without a base, inviting the reading that 10.7% of all windows (or of judged windows) were declined.

findings.fix: Say 'the 13 named stations shown hold almost all of the {F080} live scripts' or note that the station table beside the chapter carries the full set.
findings.issue: The caption says holdings total {F080} (248,841) scripts, but the 13 bars of S012 sum to 248,323; T022 carries 14 rows, so a station or remainder of 518 scripts is not shown in the chart.

findings.fix: Add one point: '{F015} tables are empty and {F014} table pairs duplicate each other across {F013} rows held; both are retirement candidates once ownership is confirmed.'
findings.issue: The chapter on database condition omits structural findings the evidence plainly carries: {F015} 368 empty tables, {F014} 71 duplicate table pairs and {F013} 259.3m rows held, all measured in R01 and relevant to the cleanup the actions propose.

findings.fix: Either state the reason (e.g. larger row count and catalogue reuse value) or order the shortlist by readiness score and keep the buyer-side review as the deciding step. Rights wording is correct and should stay as is.
findings.issue: The content catalogue corpus (readiness 56.8, grade C) is proposed as a first product ahead of channel engagement analytics (59.7) and the forecasting and transaction datasets (57.6) on the census's own readiness score; the draft calls the order a planning judgement but gives no reason for passing over higher-scoring candidates.

review.summary: Every figure is used for the quantity its label names, chapters answer their questions and the owner declarations on rights are honoured throughout; nothing would mislead the owner. The advisories concern unresolved placeholder tokens, the apparent 15.2 GiB versus 54.1 GiB database tension, an unstated base for the declined-label share, a chart-to-total gap of 518 scripts, omitted empty-table and duplicate-pair findings, and an unexplained product ordering.
